4. That upon receipt of the summons thereof this petitioner appeared before the Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on 3-2-1999 with a prayer for time to submit written statement which was allowed. Thereafter, the petitioner took several adjournments and lastly, submitted written objection on 28-3-2000. Upon hearing the parties, the Subordinate Judge was pleased to pass the impugned Order No. 14 dated 7-5-2000 and rejected the written objection holding that the same is barred by Article 158 of the Limitation Act and for not depositing security money as per provision of section 32 of the Arbitration Act of 1940 inserted by the Law Reforms Ordinance 1978 together with such written objection. 

 7. The second point raised by the learned Advocate, Mr Md Mahbubey Alam is that the Court below has failed to observe that where an award was illegal and void for want of jurisdiction of the Arbitrator to pass it, the question of filing written objection within 30 (thirty) days under Article 158 of the Limitation Act was immaterial and that in the instant case falling under section 8(a) of the Arbitration Act, 1940 the award passed by the opposite party No.2 as the sole Arbitrator was illegal, void and no award in the eye of law since, according to opposite parties No. 2's own showing in the application (plaint), he did not obtain appointment for the Court as Sole Arbitrator under section 8(2) of the Arbitration Act, 1940 and was not legally eligible to be so appointed after accepting to represent the interest of opposite party No. 1 alone as an Arbitrator over the same issue between the same parties and that the Court below failed to realise that the question of giving Security Money as per proviso of section 33 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 inserted by the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1978 arises only when the case is under section 33 of the Arbitration Act challenging the validity of an Arbitration Agreement or Award and not otherwise. 

 10. On the contrary, Mr MA Samad assisted by Mr MGH Ruhullah, the learned Advocate, submits that the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 filed a Title Suit No. 1 of 1999 on 31-1-1999, the petitioner appeared before the Court on 3-2-1999 and took several adjournments and lastly, on 28-3-2000 submitted the written objections which is barred as per Article 158 of the Limitation Act. He has further submitted that the appointment of the Sole Arbitrator was the correct procedure followed and it was done according to provisions of law. The defendant-petitioner did not willfully and intentionally respond to the notices of the Sole Arbitrator and contest the arbitration proceedings with a view to deny payment to the consultant on the plea that the claim had no legal basis and the appointment of the Arbitrator was illegal. Mr MA Samad also has taken us to section 33 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 as amended in 1978 and has contended that unless the applicant has deposited in the Court the amount which he is required to pay under the award or has furnished security to the satisfaction of the Court for the payment of such sum or for the fulfillment of any other obligation by this under the award and in the instant case the defendant-petitioner did not furnish Bank Guarantee or security as required under the provision of law under section 33 of the Arbitration Act is a nullity in the eye of law. Lastly, Mr MA Samad submits that it is a settled principle of law that an application under section 33 of the Arbitration Act rendered the said written objection under section 33 of the Arbitration Act as non-existent in the eye of law and learned Subordinate Judge rightly rejected the : written objection and there is nothing to interfere. 

 12. Admittedly, the defendant-petitioner of this revisional application appeared before the Court on 3-2-1999 and after taking several adjournments filed the written objection on 28-3-2000 which, according to Mr MA Samad, is beyond the period of 30 days and governed by Article 158 of the Limitation Act and the learned Subordinate Judge, according to him, rightly rejected the written objection of the defendant-petitioner being barred. 

 14. It appears from the record that the defendant-petitioner appeared in court on 3-2-1999 and after taking several adjournments filed the written objection on 28-3-2000 which is, in our opinion, not at all time barred. It also appears from the impugned order dated 7-5-2000 of the Court below that the Court not only rejected the written objection on the ground that the same was barred under Article 158 of the Limitation Act, but also for want of security deposit relating to the award. The order of the learned Court below is quoted is a clear bar against taking such a plea:
